entries.title: Poincare and Cheeger constants: Euclidean conventions
entries.statement: For a probability measure nu, C_P(nu) is the least coefficient in Var_nu(f)<=C_P(nu) integral |grad f|^2 dnu for locally Lipschitz L2 functions; infinite energy makes the inequality automatic. h(nu) is inf nu^+(B)/min(nu(B),1-nu(B)) over Borel sets with 0<nu(B)<1, where nu^+(B)=liminf_{epsilon down to 0}(nu(B+epsilon EuclideanBall)-nu(B))/epsilon. On a line the gradient uses Euclidean arclength. Isotropic means barycenter zero and covariance identity.

entries.title: P0017: normalized KLS target and October proof-claim status
entries.statement: The P0017 target asks for a finite universal C with C_P(mu)<=C for every dimension n>=1 and every isotropic log-concave probability on R^n; equivalently a universal positive Euclidean Cheeger lower bound. Original source: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2025, 2603.29571v1, Entry 13, Conjecture 30. On 2026-10-10 primary preprints 2610.05474v1, 2610.01447v2 and 2610.07728v2 claim full proofs; the last claims C_P<=25. This draft verifies their statement/version metadata, not their proofs. The September attempted_unsolved label cannot certify current openness. Openness UNKNOWN in this audit; no new solution or novelty claim. A partial slice lemma does not settle the parent.

entries.title: Refuted bridge: ambient isotropy bounds every line fiber
entries.statement: FALSE auxiliary claim: one finite universal B bounds C_P(mu(.|P_{u-perp}X=z)) for every dimension, every isotropic log-concave mu, every unit u, and projected-almost-every z, without restandardizing the conditional law. The isotropic-simplex edge-fiber family forces essential supremum 2(n+1)(n+2)/pi^2. This stronger bridge's failure does not refute normalized KLS.

entries.title: Isotropic simplex: exact extremes and average of edge-fiber constants
entries.statement: Author-proved special case; independent review pending. For each n>=2 an isotropic uniform regular-simplex probability mu_n and an edge-parallel unit u have orthogonal-projection fibers whose inherited-arclength constants satisfy ess sup C_P=2(n+1)(n+2)/pi^2, E C_P=12/pi^2, ess sup Var=(n+1)(n+2)/6 and E Var=1. The ess sup uses the projected law and every near-extremal range has positive mass. Each fiber itself satisfies C_P=(12/pi^2)Var, so it is the conditional covariance control that fails.
entries.proof_text: For X uniform on {x_i>=0,sum x_i<=1}, m=EX and Sigma=Cov X, let a=(n+1)(n+2), A=Sigma^{-1/2}, Y=A(X-m), u=Ae_1/sqrt(2a). Direct simplex integration gives Sigma^{-1}=a(I+J), so Y is isotropic and |Ae_1|^2=2a. The projected base fixes x_2,...,x_n; conditionally x_1 is uniform on [0,T], T=1-sum_{i>=2}x_i. Thus <u,Y> is uniform on a centered interval of length sqrt(2a)T. T has Beta(2,n-1) law, ET^2=6/a and P(T>1-epsilon)>0. Interval variance L^2/12 and sharp Poincare coefficient L^2/pi^2 give all claims. Independently represented in w355's barycentric H-space derivation and checked by w356; w356's own contribution still awaits its designated reviewer w359.
assumptions: Uniform regular simplex whitened to covariance I

entries.title: Refuted bridge: separate the average constant from fiber energy
entries.statement: FALSE auxiliary inference: E C_P(fiber)=B implies E Var(f|Z)<=B E |partial_u f|^2 for all Lipschitz f. The valid conditional inequality is E Var(f|Z)<=E[C_P(fiber) E(|partial_u f|^2|Z)]. Removing this covariance between fiber size and energy is unjustified. The isotropic-simplex cosine test family has a quotient 50.5 times B at n=100,k=10, although B=12/pi^2.

entries.title: Simplex cosine family: exact failure of unweighted fiber-energy averaging
entries.statement: Author-proved special case; independent review pending. In the preceding simplex let a=(n+1)(n+2), T=1-sum_{i>=2}X_i and f_k(Y)=T^k cos(pi X_1/T), extended by zero at T=0, for integer k>=1. It is Lipschitz and E[f_k|Z]=0. Its conditional-variance/directional-energy quotient is R(n,k)=(2a/pi^2)(2k)(2k+1)/((n+2k-1)(n+2k)). For k>1 it exceeds 12/pi^2; for n=100,k=10 its ratio to that mean fiber constant is exactly 50.5. As k grows, R tends to 2a/pi^2. No assertion uses this directional energy in place of the full gradient in KLS.
entries.proof_text: Since 0<=X_1<=T, partial derivatives of T^k cos(pi X_1/T) are bounded by constants times T^(k-1); it extends continuously and is Lipschitz on the simplex. Along u, A^{-1}u=e_1/sqrt(2a) and T is fixed. Conditional cosine mean is zero, variance is T^(2k)/2 and directional energy is pi^2 T^(2k-2)/(4a). For T~Beta(2,n-1), ET^r=(r+1)!n!/(n+r)!. Dividing the two moments proves R. At n=100,k=10, (a/6)*420/(119*120)=101/2. The transverse part of the gradient remains outside this directional calculation.
assumptions: The simplex and direction from the preceding lemma
Lipschitz extension, no C1 claim at T=0

entries.title: Uniform interval: exact Poincare, Cheeger and scale boundary
entries.statement: Independently rederived by w356 from w354's claim. Uniform probability on a Euclidean interval of length L>0 has variance L^2/12, C_P=L^2/pi^2 and h=2/L. At variance one these are C_P=12/pi^2 and h=1/sqrt(3). Arbitrary dilation therefore forbids an unnormalized universal C_P upper bound or h lower bound, without contradicting the normalized KLS target.
entries.proof_text: Integrating x and x^2 gives variance L^2/12. Even reflection of a mean-zero H1 function gives a 2L-periodic function; Parseval and the first nonzero frequency pi/L imply C_P<=L^2/pi^2. Cos(pi x/L) attains equality. A half interval has outer Minkowski perimeter 1/L and min mass 1/2. Any nontrivial Borel set either has positive closure-minus-set mass and infinite outer perimeter, or a nonempty open complement component with an interior endpoint supplies an epsilon expansion strip of length epsilon. Thus perimeter>=1/L and h>=2/L. The half interval attains the lower bound.
assumptions: Euclidean gradient and outer Minkowski perimeter

entries.title: Isotropic triangle: a smooth polynomial separates directional and full energy
entries.statement: Independently rederived by w356 from w354's polynomial claim. On the whitened uniform standard triangle, use the edge direction u from the simplex construction, T=<u,Y>, S=X_2 and f(Y)=T(1-S)^2. Then E[f|Z]=0, E Var(f|Z)=1/2, E|partial_u f|^2=1/3 and E|grad f|^2=13/27. Replacing the mean fiber constant 12/pi^2 in the directional conditional inequality would require 1/2<=4/pi^2, which is false. The full-gradient Rayleigh quotient is 27/26; this calculation does not refute KLS.
entries.proof_text: With t=1-X_2, its density is 2t and conditional Var(T|Z)=2t^2. The affine base gradient b=grad_Y S is perpendicular to u and has |b|^2=1/18. Therefore f has variance 2Et^6=1/2 and directional energy Et^4=1/3. Its full gradient is u*t^2-2*T*t*b, with zero cross term; its energy is Et^4+4|b|^2E[T^2t^2]=13/27. Independently integrating the raw polynomial f/sqrt(24)=X_1t^2-t^3/2 and its two derivatives against exact triangle monomial moments gives the same variance and full energy. Since pi>3, 4/pi^2<4/9<1/2.
assumptions: Whitened uniform triangle in dimension two
Euclidean full gradient and the specified edge direction

relations.rationale: The exact simplex constants use the declared inherited-arclength and isotropy conventions.
The positive-mass essential supremum grows quadratically with n under the bridge's ambient-isotropy assumptions.
The cosine test uses precisely that simplex, direction and beta-distributed fiber length.
Its n=100,k=10 conditional-variance/energy ratio is exactly 50.5 times the proposed average coefficient.
The sharp interval formulas use the same Poincare and Cheeger conventions.
After explicit disintegration each edge fiber is a uniform interval; its sharp interval coefficient is applied at its actual length.
Updates the audit context of the dated P0017 problem card without refuting its explicitly historical status or declaring a proof independently checked.
The exact smooth witness uses dimension two of that whitened simplex and the same edge projection.
Exact monomial integration gives 1/2 conditional variance and 1/3 directional energy, contradicting the proposed mean coefficient 12/pi^2, with the full energy separately accounted for.
